findings.title: newCheckout flag permanently false; if-branch never reachable
findings.note: FLAGS hardcodes newCheckout to false with a comment confirming it has been off since launch and the new flow was never finished. There is no runtime toggle for it in the repo, so the `new:` branch of checkout() is unreachable dead code.

findings.title: adminEnabled() has no callers and checks a flag key absent from FLAGS
findings.note: adminEnabled is exported but has zero in-repo callers, and the "adminPanel" key it checks is not present in FLAGS at all, so isEnabled falls through to its `?? false` default permanently. File is the highest-scored hotspot in the repo.

findings.title: betaBanner flag hardcoded true with no toggle path
findings.note: betaBanner is hardcoded to true in FLAGS with no other write site in the repo, so the isEnabled check in getJson always evaluates true; the conditional adds no branching value.

open_questions.question: Is the "adminPanel" key expected to be injected into FLAGS by external config/build tooling not present in this repo, or was it never wired up?
Is newCheckout expected to be revived later, or should the flag and its branch be removed given the comment says the flow was never finished?

looks_bad_but_fine.why: legacyFormat is marked @deprecated but is still actively called from src/checkout/checkout.ts:11, so it has a live in-repo caller and is not dead code.
getJson has no in-repo caller, but it is an exported function from an API client module (public/library surface), matching the entry-point exception.
getAdminJson has no in-repo caller, but like getJson it is exported public API-client surface rather than an internal dead unit.

not_assessed: Whether "adminPanel" is read from an external config/env system outside this repo (dynamic reference via string key cannot be fully ruled out from static search alone)
Test coverage, CVE/vulnerability status, or dependency currency were not evaluated
